estimationMethod.name: 3-Station Inverse Distance Weighting (IDW, p = 2) → CPCB National AQI Standard
estimationMethod.formulaSummary: Ĉ_pollutant(x₀) = Σ [wᵢ · C_pollutant(xᵢ)] / Σ wᵢ, where wᵢ = 1 / max(dᵢ, 1 km)^2 across the k = 3 nearest CPCB stations; AQI = max(I_PM2.5, I_PM10, I_NO2, I_CO, I_O3).
estimationMethod.concentrationFirstNote: Individual criteria pollutant concentrations (PM2.5, PM10, NO₂, CO, O₃) are spatially interpolated first; the official CPCB piecewise-linear breakpoint sub-index formula is applied only after concentration estimation.
estimationMethod.externalInputsRoleNote: Satellite atmospheric observations and meteorological weather readings are retrieved live and displayed separately for environmental context. They do not modify the numerical concentration weights because live atmospheric model timestamps are asynchronous with the reference CPCB station readings and directional wind-weighting did not reduce out-of-sample error during calibration.
steps: Resolved verified WGS84 coordinates for Haveri, Karnataka (14.7935°N, 75.4045°E).
Selected the 3 nearest suitable CPCB monitoring stations and verified airshed proximity bounds (d₁ ≤ 260 km, d₃ ≤ 350 km).
Interpolated PM2.5, PM10, NO₂, CO, and O₃ concentrations using validated IDW exponent p = 2.
Calculated pollutant sub-indices and overall AQI using the CPCB Indian AQI breakpoint standard (minimum 3 pollutants including PM2.5 or PM10).

uncertainty.method: Split-Conformal Prediction Interval (calibrated on 72-station multi-date training residuals, validated on 71 held-out stations)

validationSummary.methodName: Concentration-First Inverse Distance Weighting (IDW, k=3, p=2) + CPCB Breakpoint Standard

xaiInterpretation.vegetation: Coastal hills and tree canopies generate diffuse volume backscattering, translated into lush emerald-to-lime green hues with natural canopy micro-textures.
xaiInterpretation.water: Smooth bay and canal water bodies produce specular radar reflection away from the sensor (dark backscatter), rendered as deep sapphire blue with luminous turquoise coastal shallows.
xaiInterpretation.buildingsAndRoads: Orthogonal facades, stadium geodesic dome struts, and street networks produce intense double-bounce specular corner reflections, translated to vibrant terracotta, amber, copper, and crisp concrete white highlights.
xaiInterpretation.bareLand: Sandy shoreline buffers and engineered breakwaters display intermediate dielectric roughness, mapped to golden sand tones.
xaiInterpretation.backscatterPhysics: Umbra sub-meter spotlight SAR and Sentinel-1 C-band dual-pol (VV/VH) reveal fine structural boundaries, stadium geometry, and coastal-urban transitions under all-weather day/night conditions.
xaiInterpretation.vvVhRatio: VV/VH ratio calculated at 7.82 dB, characteristic of dense engineered metropolitan topography and stadium architecture.
